info.title: Counted API
info.description: Privacy-first product analytics. No cookies, no fingerprinting, no PII. Identity is optional and always supplied by the caller.

ingestKey.name: Project-Key
ingestKey.description: A public ingest credential. Safe to embed; grants events:write and nothing else.

serviceKey.description: A secret service credential, scoped to the operations it was issued for.

shareToken.description: A share link token (st_…). Read-only, bound to one dashboard and the projects its tiles read, and expiring.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, not on status or prose.

Predicate.description: A filter expression. Leaves compare a field; `and`/`or`/`not` compose them. Ordering comparisons (gt/gte/lt/lte) take a number, which is what lets the compiler emit a guarded numeric cast.

secret.description: Shown exactly once and never retrievable. Store it now.

token.description: Shown exactly once and never retrievable.

url.description: Where to send the browser. Short-lived.

get.description: Is this process running? Never touches the database, so a database blip cannot cause a restart loop.
Can this instance serve traffic? Pings the store and reports what it verified at boot.

post.description: Mails a single-use link. Answers 202 for any valid address whether or not an account exists — telling the two apart would be an oracle for discovering who uses Counted. Signing up and signing in are one flow.

202.description: The link has been sent, if the address can receive mail.

post.description: Spends the token once and sets an HttpOnly session cookie on the registrable domain, so the console and the API share it. An unknown token and an expired one are refused identically.

401.description: The link is expired, spent, or was never issued

delete.description: Ends this session and clears the cookie. Succeeds even if the session had already expired.

post.description: Accepts up to 50 events. Resolves only after the batch is durably committed, so a 202 means the data is written. Every event gets its own outcome, and the quota state is named rather than implied.

400.description: The batch could not be read

403.description: The credential may not write events

post.description: Answers one question — an analysis, a funnel or a retention grid. The response is tagged with its shape; the caller never has to infer it.

400.description: The analysis is not well formed

403.description: The credential may not read this project

post.description: Answers every tile on a dashboard in one batch. A tile that fails comes back as a failed readout rather than as an empty one, so a broken query is distinguishable from a project with no events.

post.description: Authenticated by HMAC signature over the raw body with a five-minute window, not by a credential. Deduplicated by event id: a replay is acknowledged and changes nothing. An event we do not act on is acknowledged rather than retried.
